notes.text: shall be for burning Boots, garments, weapons, chariots, and other items used during a holy war were not to become part of the booty or spoil of the victors. Such property was under a ban had to be burned with fire (Joshua 7:23-26; 11:6; Psalms 46:9; Ezekiel 39:9-10).

notes.text: government . . . upon . . . shoulder --The ensign of office used to be worn on the shoulder, in token of sustaining the government (Isa 22:22). Here the government on Messiah's shoulder is in marked antithesis to the "yoke and staff" of the oppressor on Israel's "shoulder" (Isa 9:4).

notes.text: sycamores --growing abundantly on the low lands of Judea, and though useful for building on account of their antiseptic property (which induced the Egyptians to use them for the cases of their mummies), not very valuable. The cedar, on the other hand, was odorous, free from knots, durable, and precious (1 Kings 10:27).
bricks --in the East generally sun-dried, and therefore soon dissolved by rain.
